quarterly_data.signal: Half-year 2026 report, immunology pipeline: the RELIEVE UCCD long-term extension showed duvakitug's clinical and endoscopic efficacy maintained over 44 weeks in ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease responders (now in phase 3); lunsekimig met its primary and key secondary endpoints in the AIRCULES phase 2b study in moderate-to-severe asthma and the DUET phase 2a study in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, while the exploratory VELVET phase 2b study in atopic dermatitis missed its primary endpoint (lunsekimig is in phase 3 in COPD); the FREXERA phase 2/3 study of frexalimab in kidney transplantation dosed its first patient in March 2026. Japan approved Dupixent for moderate-to-severe bullous pemphigoid, while Sanofi withdrew the EU application for Dupixent in bullous pemphigoid after EMA comments during the review.
quarterly_data.figure: duvakitug efficacy maintained over 44 weeks; lunsekimig AIRCULES and DUET met primary endpoints, VELVET missed; FREXERA first patient March 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Half-year 2026 report, rare disease, cardiometabolic and vaccines: Cytokinetics, Sanofi's licensor of Myqorzo (aficamten) in China, reported positive ACACIA-HCM phase 3 results in non-obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (all primary endpoints met), expected to support a China submission in 2027; Redemplo (plozasiran, marketed in Greater China under an agreement with Arrowhead) received a breakthrough designation in China in severe hypertriglyceridemia, with a launch in familial chylomicronaemia syndrome planned in the near future; efdoralprin alfa holds US fast track designation. Nuvaxovid showed statistically significant lower systemic reactogenicity than Moderna's mNEXSPIKE across all pre-specified endpoints in the COMPARE study (1,000 US adults); the FDA and EMA accepted for review the Fluzone HD/Efluelda submission for adults aged 50 and above (QHD00042 phase 3); and the Democratic Republic of the Congo approved acoziborole for sleeping sickness. The registration-stage pipeline lists venglustat (Gaucher disease type 3; US, EU, JP), Sarclisa SC (China), Fluzone HD (US, EU) and SP0087 rabies vaccine (EU).
quarterly_data.figure: ACACIA-HCM all primary endpoints met (China submission 2027); COMPARE 1,000 adults; Fluzone HD 50+ under FDA/EMA review

quarterly_data.signal: Half-year 2026 financial detail: net income attributable to equity holders was EUR 1,957 million vs EUR 5,812 million (EPS EUR 1.63 vs EUR 4.74), after impairment of intangible assets of EUR 1,031 million, mainly a EUR 952 million impairment of the amlitelimab asset (its entire carrying amount), which also lifted the effective tax rate to 30.6%. Dupixent sales were EUR 9,324 million (+34.4% CER; United States EUR 6,922 million, +39.5% CER); Ayvakit sales were EUR 367 million, and without the increased US rebates that followed the Blueprint integration its revenue growth would have been approximately nine percentage points higher; Tzield/Teizeild has treated over 1,000 patients; US net sales were EUR 11,633 million (+29.9% CER) and China EUR 1,325 million (-3.5% CER). At July 2026 average exchange rates, currency impacts on the 2026 outlook are estimated at approximately -1% on sales and -2% on business EPS.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 net income EUR 1,957 million; amlitelimab impairment EUR 952 million; H1 Dupixent EUR 9,324 million (+34.4% CER); FX approximately -1% sales, -2% business EPS

quarterly_data.signal: In-licensing deals disclosed in the half-year report: in March 2026 Sanofi took an exclusive worldwide license to develop, manufacture and commercialize rovadicitinib (first-in-class oral JAK/ROCK inhibitor, approved first in China in February 2026 for first-line myelofibrosis) from CTTQ, a Sino Biopharmaceutical subsidiary, for a $135 million upfront payment, up to $1.4 billion in development, regulatory and sales milestones and tiered royalties up to double digits; also in March 2026 it licensed worldwide rights to KT501, a tri-specific T-cell engager for autoimmune diseases, from Kali Therapeutics for up to $1.2 billion including upfront payments ($0.1 billion already paid) plus tiered royalties.
quarterly_data.figure: rovadicitinib: $135 million upfront, up to $1.4 billion milestones; KT501: up to $1.2 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Portfolio moves: the Dynavax acquisition closed on February 10, 2026, adding the US-marketed two-dose adult hepatitis B vaccine HEPLISAV-B and the Z-1018 shingles vaccine candidate (phase 1/2); Dynavax contributed EUR 144 million of net sales and EUR 89 million of business operating income since the acquisition date. On March 6, 2026 Sanofi agreed to sell Medley, its Brazilian generics business, to EMS Group; closing is expected no earlier than the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to CADE antitrust clearance, with a net gain expected. Biopharma acquisitions of property, plant and equipment were EUR 763 million in the half (Manufacturing & Supply EUR 594 million), with firm orders for property, plant and equipment of EUR 1,336 million at June 30, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Dynavax EUR 144 million net sales since acquisition; Medley sale closing no earlier than Q4 2026; firm PP&E orders EUR 1,336 million
